questions.question: Define the fashion cycle. a). Laundry process b). Life span of a fashion trend c). Circular sewing technique d). Production method / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Formal Wear:
  • Formal wear is designed for professional or official occasions. It
  • emphasizes a polished, elegant, and professional appearance, often
  • adhering to workplace or event-specific dress codes. Formal wear is
  • usually neutral in color (black, white, gray, navy) and features minimal
  • patterns. Accessories like belts or simple jewelry enhance the
  • professional look. Common Garments are blazers, trousers, pencil skirts,
  • formal shirts, business suits.
  • Examples:
  • Polyester: Lightweight, wrinkle-resistant fabric used in blazers and
  • formal trousers. Example: Office blazer.
  • Cotton Poplin: Smooth, crisp fabric used in button-down formal shirts.
  • Example: White formal shirt worn in offices.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

questions.question: Explain the fashion trend? a). A permanent style b). A popular style accepted by many people at a time c). A traditional costume d). A marketing technique / [CO2]
questions.solution_html:
• Ethnic Wear
  • Ethnic wear includes traditional clothing inspired by cultural heritage. It
  • is worn during festivals, weddings, or culturally significant events.
  • Common Garments are Sarees, salwar suits, lehengas, kurtis, dupattas.
  • Ethnic wear often features embroidery, prints, or embellishments
  • reflecting regional craftsmanship. Colors are usually vibrant and designs
  • culturally significant.
  • Examples:
  • Silk: Luxurious, smooth fabric for festive sarees or lehengas. Example:
  • Kanjivaram silk saree for weddings.
  • Cotton (Handloom / Khadi): Breathable, lightweight fabric for summer
  • kurtis or casual ethnic sets. Example: Cotton salwar suit for daily wear.
questions.source_exam: First Semester MGU-UGP/MGU-BBA/MGU-BCA Honours Examinations November 2025

• Party Wear
  • Party wear is designed for social events, evening parties, or celebrations. It
  • emphasizes glamour, style, and elegance. Common Garments are Gowns,
  • sequinned dresses, cocktail dresses, fancy tops, jumpsuits. Party wear often
  • incorporates bold colors, metallics, sequins, beads, or lace. It focuses on
  • enhancing the wearer’s appearance for special occasions and making a fashion
  • statementExamples:
  • Satin: Smooth, glossy fabric giving a luxurious look, often used in
  • evening gowns. Example: Satin cocktail dress.
  • Georgette: Lightweight, flowy fabric suitable for draped dresses or tops.
  • Example: Embellished georgette party gown.

questions.question: State the main purposes of clothing and explain briefly each one. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• State the main purposes of clothing and explain briefly each one.
  • ANS: Clothing is manufactured of fibre and textile, material worn on the body.
  • Clothing perform a range of social and cultural functions, such as individual,
  • occupational and sexual differentiation and social status. Clothing also function
  • as a form of adornement and an expression of personal taste or style.
  • PROTECTION:Clothes provide humans a source of physical protection even
  • before clothing evolved as a means of protection against the physical dangers of
  • natural calamity, evil, spirits, Demons, and spiritual powers. The type of
  • clothing was in the form of jewellery tattooing etc..
  • COMMUNICATION: Clothing communicates various facts of a person’s life
  • such as age, sex, lifestyle, occupation, religious beliefs. Clothing reflects our
  • value system, attitudes, interest in life. Clothing also conveys self-image,
  • emotions, et cetera.
  • DECORATION: Even before the invention of clothes, people adorn their bodies
  • with body painting, tattooing, piercing and hairstyling. Therefore, adornment in
  • clothing, enhance one’s self image through beautification, improving sexual
  • attraction and establishing social status.

questions.question: Define the purpose of clothing and list its various functions. / [CO1]
questions.solution_html:
• Define the purpose of clothing and list its various functions.
  • ANS: Clothing is manufactured of fibre and textile, material worn on the body.
  • The most obvious function of clothing is to improve the comfort of the wearer
  • by protecting the wearer. Clothing perform a range of social and cultural
  • functions, such as individual, occupational and sexual differentiation and social
  • status. Clothing also function as a form of adornement and an expression of
  • personal taste or style.
  • PROTECTION:Clothes provide humans a source of physical protection even
  • before clothing evolved as a means of protection against the physical dangers of
  • natural calamity, evil, spirits, Demons, and spiritual powers. The type of
  • clothing was in the form of jewellery tattooing etc..
  • Then came the clothes made from animal skins and part of trees including their
  • bark to protect the body from excessive heat, cold and bites and stings of insects
  • and animals. In today times, clothes, For example, raincoat, gloves, draper,
  • thermal, suits, and sports gear for the sake of protecting our bodies.
  • Protection from cold- Wear multiple layers of clothing, thick, or heavy fabrics.
  • Fur Lining:Trap body heat and create a layer of warmth.
  • Gloves and mittens: Protect the fingers from frost bites.
  • Specialised forms of protective clothing: Diving suits, space suits, firefighters,
  • attire, bullet-proof, jackets, facial masks.
  • Protective gears- helmets, gloves, diving, suits, water googles.
  • COMMUNICATION: Clothing communicates various facts of a person’s life
  • such as age, sex, lifestyle, occupation, religious beliefs. Clothing reflects our
  • value system, attitudes, interest in life. Clothing also conveys self-image,
  • emotions, et cetera.
  • Age: Example college student of wears, T-shirt and jeans, they change to shirts
  • and trousers in the case of an office goer.
  • Sex: Men shirts buttoned leftover right and woman right over left.
  • Marital status: Hindu woman wear mangalsutra and Sindoor.
  • Cultural influences: The traditional dress of the Japanese,the kimono, reflects
  • the culture, customs and traditions of the Japanese people.
  • DECORATION: Even before the invention of clothes, people adorn their bodies
  • with body painting, tattooing, piercing and hairstyling. Therefore, adornment in
  • clothing, enhance one’s self image through beautification, improving sexual
  • attraction and establishing social status.
